title: German Expressionism
description: German Expressionism cinematography treats the set as a mind: forced-perspective corridors, painted shadows, and jagged hard light replace natural architecture. The camera is often locked and slightly dutch, so the actor walks a geometry that already looks illegal.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Psychology is built, not implied. A staircase leans.
A shadow is bigger than the body that casts it, and sometimes the shadow is paint. The face is lit like a mask because the room is already a diagnosis.
It is the wrong tool for a real wet street or a fashion interior. Noir keeps plausible cities and lets Hard Light do the violence.
Giallo bends color, not carpentry. If the walls are square and only the grade is moody, you do not have expressionism.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Build or paint impossible architecture: converging walls, oversized windows, stairs that refuse the horizon. Light with hard, unfilled sources so shadows are graphic edges, not soft falloff.
Dutch the camera a few degrees as a default, not a sting. Orthochromatic or high-contrast black-and-white, 35mm spherical, theatrical blocking, often locked-off.
Prompt painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged light, and Caligari psychology as set.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when the location must be a mental state, not a real address. Do not use it as a dutch-angle garnish on a square contemporary room.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: German Expressionism distorts carpentry. Film Noir distorts with light on real streets.
Dutch Angle is one tilted horizon; expressionism is the whole set. Hard Light is the source quality.
Chiaroscuro is the ratio. You need the bent architecture, not only the contrast.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is Film Noir or a lone Dutch Angle: a wet alley, or a tilted camera in an ordinary room. The tell is square architecture with only contrast added.
Fix: cant the set or the perspective, paint or project graphic shadows, and lock the camera on that geometry.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is German Expressionism in film?
A look in which distorted sets, painted or graphic shadows, hard unfilled light, and stylized blocking make the location a psychological diagram rather than a real street.
German Expressionism vs Film Noir
Noir keeps plausible cities and cuts them with gobos. Expressionism rebuilds the city as a bent mind. Both love hard light. Only one makes the staircase illegal.
When should I use German Expressionism?
When a character's inner state has to be walked through as architecture. Skip it for crime on real wet streets, for gelled fashion-horror, or for a dutch angle with nothing else changed.
How do I prompt German Expressionism for AI image or video?

Write: German expressionist treatment of [Subject], painted shadows, impossible architecture, jagged hard light, dutch horizon. Specify the illegal wall or stair. Do not prompt a normal room plus contrast.
